import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided by the user
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# --- Visualization ---

# Set a professional and clean style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a bubble chart using seaborn's scatterplot
# X-axis: Price
# Y-axis: Megapixels
# Bubble Size: Max ISO (representing low-light capability)
# Color: Brand
# Marker Style: Body Type
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    size='max_iso',
    sizes=(200, 2000),  # Control the min and max size of bubbles
    hue='brand',
    style='body_type',
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1,
    ax=ax,
    legend='full' # Show all legend elements
)

# --- Annotations and Customization ---

# Add text labels for each point for better identification
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.text(
        row['price_usd'] + 50,  # Offset the text slightly to the right
        row['megapixels'],
        f"{row['brand']} '{str(row['model_year'])[-2:]}\n{row['sensor_type']}",
        fontsize=9,
        fontstyle='italic',
        verticalalignment='center'
    )

# Set plot title and axis labels
ax.set_title('Camera Market Analysis: Price, Megapixels, and ISO Capability', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=12)

# Format the x-axis to show dollar signs and commas
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%.0f')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Improve the legend
# Move the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap
h, l = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate the legends for clarity (e.g., one for Brand, one for Body Type, one for ISO)
plt.legend(h, l, bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0., title='Legend')


# Adjust layout to make sure everything fits
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Make room for the legend on the right

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Close the plot to free memory
plt.close()
